title: SHADOW Arsenal profile manifest
description: One security tool profile. Checked by arsenal/tools/validate.py, which implements the keywords used here and adds the cross-file rules listed in arsenal/docs/adding-tools.md (category ids from categories.json, unique packages, resolvable includes).

id.description: Profile identifier; equals the file name without .json.

summary.description: One line shown on the profile card.

description.description: A few sentences: what the profile is for and who would install it.

icon.description: Icon-theme name of the profile icon (assets/icons/categories/<name>.svg or assets/icons/apps/<name>.svg).

metapackage.description: Binary package that depends on the tools of this profile; always shadow-arsenal-<id>.

includes.description: Ids of other profiles whose tools belong to this one as well. The tools are referenced, never copied.

tools.description: Tools installed from Debian main (or the SHADOW security repository) through the package manager.

external.description: Well-known tools that are NOT installable from the configured repositories. The manager lists them with a link; nothing is downloaded or repackaged.

url.description: Upstream/homepage URL. https is preferred; a few upstream sites are http-only.

package.description: Debian binary package name, verified by tools/check-availability.py.

name.description: Name people know the tool by.

summary.description: One line, no trailing full stop.

architectures.description: Only if the package does not exist on every supported architecture.

command.description: Executable shipped by the package, for 'Open in terminal'. Required for cli and both.

help.description: Argument vector (one element per item) that makes the command print its usage. Default: ['--help'].

desktop-id.description: Desktop entry shipped by the package (without .desktop), for 'Open'. Required for gui and both.

notes.description: Anything the user should know before installing or running the tool.

packages.description: Optional. Debian binary package names this tool would have. tools/check-availability.py confirms that none of them is in trixie main (if one appears, the tool moves to 'tools').

license.description: Licence of the tool and any restriction that matters for redistribution or use.

why.description: Why SHADOW does not offer a package.

how.description: Where the vendor or upstream project says to get it. Text plus the official URL; never a command that pipes a download into a shell.
